answer: A fraud-proof window over escrowed funds sets cost per identity: 80 units lock for 30 days while its log grows as a vine carrying a marker from its key, and a summit checkpoint closes each epoch. Auditors replay the vine at the summit and set a pulse nonce to sign in 60 seconds; proof that one marker signed two pulse replies, or one unit backs two accounts, slashes the escrow and zeroes weights. One honest agent locks 80 units once and recovers them in 30 days. A farm with 1,000 fakes must lock 80,000 units, because one deposit and marker cannot serve two accounts without leaving that proof.
